The gonadosomatic index (GSI) of the Goatee croaker (Dendrophysa russelii) has been reported at 5% [GSI = 5%] at a water temperature of 28.3 °C [T = 28.3 °C]. This measurement was obtained under controlled laboratory conditions at a stable water temperature of 28.3 °C [T = 28.3 °C]. The value implies that reproductive investment per spawning event is not maximized, which may be an adaptation to extended spawning seasons rather than a single, explosive pulse of gamete release. This relatively conservative ovarian investment likely reflects an energetic trade-off between maintaining somatic condition and producing successive batches of pelagic eggs over several months.

Eggs of the Goatee croaker are pelagic and relatively small, with a mean diameter of 0.9 millimeters, which yields a calculated wet weight at birth of approximately 0.00039 grams [Wwb = approximately 0.00039 grams]. This value is derived from the spherical volume formula applied to the average egg diameter. Such a diminutive initial mass is typical of marine teleosts that produce large numbers of small, planktonic eggs as part of a broadcast spawning strategy. Hatching of these embryonated eggs occurs remarkably quickly under optimal thermal conditions at 28.3 °C [T = 28.3 °C], with an age at birth of 4 days [ab = 4 days] recorded. This rapid embryonic development is characteristic of warm-water sciaenids and contrasts markedly with the prolonged incubation periods observed in temperate or cold-water congeners. The combination of small egg size and swift eclosion allows emerging yolk-sac larvae to enter the planktonic environment at a very early developmental stage, where they must quickly commence exogenous feeding to fuel their subsequent growth and survival.

Sexual maturation in Dendrophysa russelii is closely tied to body size rather than strictly to chronological age, and a key size threshold is the total length at puberty, recorded at 19 centimeters [Lp = 19 centimeters]. Individuals reaching this length are considered to have initiated gonadal recrudescence and to be capable of vitellogenesis and spermiation. The corresponding wet weight at puberty is estimated at approximately 5,000 grams [Wwp = approximately 5,000 grams], a considerable mass that reflects the substantial somatic growth required before reproductive activity can commence. This size-based maturation pattern is common among larger sciaenid fishes, where early reproduction at a small body size would likely result in reduced fecundity and lower offspring survival. The pronounced difference between the weight at puberty and the tiny weight at birth underscores the extensive period of juvenile growth that must be completed before an individual can contribute to the next generation. Comparative data from other sciaenids in the genus Argyrosomus suggest that the length at first maturity can vary with local environmental conditions and fishing pressure.

The ultimate total length attained by Goatee croaker has been documented at 38.3 centimeters [Li = 38.3 centimeters], which represents the asymptotic size approached by fully grown adults in the wild. Corresponding to this maximum length, the ultimate wet weight has been calculated at approximately 103,000 grams [Wwi = approximately 103,000 grams], derived from a length-weight relationship specific to the species. This impressive body size places Dendrophysa russelii among the larger members of its family in the Indo-West Pacific region. The maximum lifespan recorded for this species is 15 years [am = 15 years], a longevity that was observed in individuals maintained under stable thermal conditions at 28.3 °C [T = 28.3 °C]. Such a long life expectancy is characteristic of slow-growing, late-maturing sciaenids that invest in somatic maintenance and iterative reproduction over many seasons. The combination of a large ultimate size and a decadal lifespan suggests a life-history strategy oriented toward persistence and repeated spawning events rather than a single, high-risk reproductive bout. Older individuals may also attain greater fecundity due to increased body cavity volume.

Reproductive output in the Goatee croaker is substantial, with actively spawning females producing multiple batches of pelagic eggs throughout an extended breeding season. Fecundity per spawning event has been estimated at approximately 1,500,000 eggs per batch [N_R_i = approximately 1,500,000 eggs per batch], a value indicative of a highly fecund broadcast spawner. These females may release several such batches over the course of a single spawning season, with a documented spawning frequency of roughly 6 events per year [F_R_i = roughly 6 events per year]. The daily reproduction rate, therefore, reflects a combination of large clutch sizes and relatively frequent spawning activity. This high fecundity is typical of marine fishes that produce pelagic larvae subject to extremely high rates of planktonic mortality, where only a tiny fraction of offspring survive to settlement. The energetic cost of producing such vast numbers of eggs is substantial and is likely supported by the large body size and high ingestion rates of adult females. The reproductive strategy of Dendrophysa russelii thus aligns closely with the classic r-selected paradigm observed in many commercially important sciaenid stocks.
